note:
v1, ON ITS HINGE (track eleven, drawn empty; whole-song skeleton). One B-flat guitar riff that a drummer can walk through two ways: six quick steps at 144 or four broad ones at 96 in the same twelve eighths. The tempo map does not change. At 1:00 a different backbeat is all that happens. For the ten seconds either side I checked the written guitars, bass, organ and kick, including lengths and accents: identical after shifting the timestamps. The hat falls from 24 hits to 16, the snare from 12 to 8. This is not a claim that two rendered takes are sample-identical.
The tell in the riff is two short pedal strokes into D-flat, then a late F. The opening picks out the ringing notes as guitar harmonics. At 0:40 the harmonium already breathes four times to the riff, ahead of the drummer. At 1:30 the guitars leave it the answer notes. A heavier second riff puts the chords just ahead of the feet. At 2:20 the drummer starts switching counts after four phrases, then two, then one. The open notes of the first riff come back as chords before the final D-flat, C, B-flat.

- When the heavy guitars stop (1:26), the harmonium plays their answer: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-onitshinge-v1-bellows.mp3

WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): 3:25 of score, 3:29 with tail. Compscore 96.83 / 93.04 (seeds 0 / 11); both −10.0 LUFS, −1.29 dBTP. The quick and broad sections either side of the change read −10.4 LUFS each on seed 0. I kept an opening from which the band enters 6.0 LU louder, against 10.4 in the first full draft; it no longer leans over 1 dB to one side. This cost some recurrence score, especially on seed 11.
The bellows use the engine's pump on a dotted quarter, not a change of playback speed. Against the identical unpumped organ, the dip and recovery repeat each 625 ms. Unmastered, in stereo, the kept organ sits 9.3/9.4 dB under the band around the hinge (12.4/12.6 under in the lower, quieter draft), then 5.8 under when playing the answers exposed. Cost: at 250–500 Hz, two short windows at the hinge are 3.7/2.8 dB over the reference-record median in the mono sum. No master EQ used to hide it.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the drummer changes the listener's footing or just seems to skip hits; whether the bellows let you hear the broad count in advance. No new card and no existing clip replaced.
NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.
SWITCH: first release. C10T11_PUMP="" keeps the reed organ without the rhythmic dip; C10T11_REED="" removes the organ.
next: Keep the ten-second matched phrases either side of 1:00 as the control for the two beats. A next composer might give the second riff at 1:50 its own short reply from the floor tom before the changes start at 2:20. Listen before treating the harmonium as muddy. Any climber.

note:
v2, THE NEXT FOOTFALL (palette, as drawn). The heavy riff at 1:50 gets ten seconds to itself. For the next four phrases, a low kettledrum answers its D-flat, F and C on the next broad beat. The guitar notes sit on sixteenths 3, 11 and 20 of the phrase; the mallet lands at 6, 12 and 24. It repeats the pitches, not the rhythm: the replies wait three, one and four sixteenths. Every fourth phrase the F folds down to C on both instruments. At 2:10 the guitars release the chords just before the drum hits, and they and the bass drop the last C entirely. That C is the drummer’s to land on the following downbeat. The last one opens the section at 2:20 where the drummer starts switching feet.

The matched guitar, bass, organ and kick phrases at 1:00 remain unchanged as written; the sections either side still match in level (−10.3 LUFS each, seed 0). I kept the low-register bench and turned it down 4 dB. All benches used the same short release and reduced hall. In the first 160 ms of each hit its raw stereo K-weighted level is 6.3 dB below the mix across the first dozen and 4.5 below across the last dozen (medians). With the same low notes at −3 dB gain it was only 3.7/2.4 below; the octave-up bench there put the 120–250 Hz share 5.1 dB above v1 during the handoff. Kept low at −7 dB, that band is up 1.4 dB from v1, 2–4 kHz is down 2.4. The last ten seconds before 2:20 are 1.3 LU quieter than v1, so the band has somewhere to return from. Scores 96.98 / 93.22 for seeds 0 / 11 (v1 96.83 / 93.04); −10.0 LUFS, −1.29 dBTP both. The MP3s have 0.7 dB extra encoding headroom, the same on both halves of the comparison.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the replies read as the drummer picking up the tune or just low-end weight; whether the beat at 2:20 feels earned. No question was waiting on this track. No card added and no old clip replaced.

note:
v4, COUNT BACK IN (section round, w7). When the drummer changed feet near the end, every guitarist used to attack the next downbeat too. Now, at the last five switches, the inner pair holds a low B-flat and the F or C from the outgoing riff straight across that downbeat. The outside pair and the bass wait. The kick counts three at 144 or two at 96: either way, the band has the same 1.25 seconds to wait. All four guitars and the bass strike with the kick halfway through the new phrase. For the quick riff, its anticipated chord moves one sixteenth later so it hits that meeting; its release stays where it was. No new player or tempo change.
